initial.name: aether_call
initial.description: Call one native AetherShell builtin with positional JSON arguments and return its typed result. `builtin` is one flat native name (`ls`, `crypto_hash`, `json_parse`); find names with `aether_discover`. Arguments are data, never AetherShell source: a string containing `${` is rejected because the interpreter would interpolate it as code, and every object key must be a plain identifier because the interpreter writes keys unquoted. A process-capable builtin runs under this call's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than reads, network, or process control; the interpreter's own `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. When a job registry and live owning agent are available and promoteOnTimeout is enabled, timeoutMs bounds only the foreground wait: expiry returns the original job id without stopping or repeating the operation. Collect its final canonical JSON outcome with job_output; use job_kill to stop it. executionTimeoutMs is the independent hard runtime limit, also capped by the deployment's maxBackgroundRuntimeMs. Omitted hard limits mean no outer runtime cap when that deployment cap is zero; native proc_run timeout_ms is unchanged. Explicit call cancellation stops and awaits the owned run. Without ownership/jobs, with promotion disabled, or if admission is refused before execution, the foreground wait remains a kill deadline. A result over the deployment's complete-result budget is retained whole and returned as an id you read with `aether_result_page`, which never runs the program again; when this deployment cannot retain it, the call fails loudly and names the narrowing remedy instead of returning a partial value. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this call: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

builtin.description: Flat native builtin name, for example "ls" or "crypto_hash".

args.description: Positional arguments in the order the builtin's signature declares them; JSON data only.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Foreground wait in milliseconds, capped by maxTimeoutMs. With job ownership and promotion enabled, expiry hands off the same execution; otherwise it is a kill deadline.

executionTimeoutMs.description: Independent positive hard execution deadline in milliseconds. Omitted, only maxBackgroundRuntimeMs applies (zero means no outer cap). Native proc_run timeout_ms remains independent.

initial.name: aether_discover
initial.description: Read the native AetherShell ontology. Without `query`, return one page of the category manifest with each category's builtin count and effect classes. With a category name, return one page of that category's builtins with their signatures and effects. With a builtin name, return its parameters, return type, effects, aliases, and examples. A name the ontology does not know returns the interpreter's own unknown-name reply, which is a successful result rather than a failure. Page a list with `offset` and `limit`; a page that leaves entries behind reports `nextOffset`. Foreground only, under a hard deadline.

query.description: Ontology category or builtin name to describe (for example "Crypto" or "crypto_hash"). Omit for the category manifest.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first entry to return (default 0). Continue a list with the previous page's nextOffset.

limit.description: Maximum entries in this page; the deployment's ontology-entry budget caps it.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin kills the interpreter. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_eval
initial.description: Evaluate one AetherShell program and return its canonical JSON value. Unlike the other tools, the program runs on the interpreter's own command line, so lambdas, modules such as `file.read("notes.txt")`, and multi-statement programs work and are not limited to flat builtin names. The program must exit successfully for a value; a failing program returns the interpreter's own error text. A program that prints nothing reports `resultType: "none"`. Everything the program does runs under this call's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control. The interpreter's `sh` switch starts off, but that is a convenience default rather than a boundary, because the program can change its own environment and reach the process builtins either way. Numbers outside the exact integer range this runtime can carry are rejected rather than rounded, so ask for such a value as text. When a job registry and live owning agent are available and promoteOnTimeout is enabled, timeoutMs bounds only the foreground wait: expiry returns the original job id without stopping or repeating the operation. Collect its final canonical JSON outcome with job_output; use job_kill to stop it. executionTimeoutMs is the independent hard runtime limit, also capped by the deployment's maxBackgroundRuntimeMs. Omitted hard limits mean no outer runtime cap when that deployment cap is zero; native proc_run timeout_ms is unchanged. Explicit call cancellation stops and awaits the owned run. Without ownership/jobs, with promotion disabled, or if admission is refused before execution, the foreground wait remains a kill deadline. A result over the deployment's complete-result budget is retained whole and returned as an id you read with `aether_result_page`, which never runs the program again; when this deployment cannot retain it, the call fails loudly and names the narrowing remedy instead of returning a partial value. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this call: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

code.description: AetherShell program text: an expression, a lambda, or a sequence of statements.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Foreground wait in milliseconds, capped by maxTimeoutMs. With job ownership and promotion enabled, expiry hands off the same execution; otherwise it is a kill deadline.

executionTimeoutMs.description: Independent positive hard execution deadline in milliseconds. Omitted, only maxBackgroundRuntimeMs applies (zero means no outer cap). Native proc_run timeout_ms remains independent.

initial.name: aether_job_start
initial.description: Start one AetherShell program as a background job and return its job id immediately. This is the streaming counterpart of `aether_eval`: the program runs on the interpreter's own command line, but no result document is read, so a program that prints logs, mixed JSON, or nothing at all still completes. Read the interpreter's raw stdout and stderr with `job_output`; the canonical exit facts and any spill file arrive with the first read after settlement. `job_kill` requests a stop; settlement follows managed-process cleanup. Each job is a fresh interpreter process: no variables, functions, or directory changes persist. The job runs without a deadline unless this deployment caps job runtime or the call supplies `timeoutMs`. The job belongs to this session and is stopped when this session's agent is disposed or the plugin unloads. Output a program's own children produce through the interpreter's process builtins may be captured by the interpreter until it returns it, so realtime child logs are not promised. The job uses this session's DSH file policy as it stood when the job started, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control; the interpreter's `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this job: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

code.description: AetherShell program text to run in the background: an expression, a lambda, or a sequence of statements.

label.description: Short human-facing label for this job, shown in job listings and the UI. Omit to use the program's first line.

cwd.description: Working directory for this job. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds for the whole job. Omitted, the job runs until it finishes or `job_kill` stops it, bounded only by this deployment's job-runtime cap when one is set.

initial.name: aether_pipeline
initial.description: Run an ordered native AetherShell pipeline, each step calling one flat builtin and feeding its result to the next. `select` maps each item of that step's result through a dotted field path, so `select: "name"` reads the `name` field of every element. `predicate` is an AetherShell expression passed to that step's builtin as its lambda first argument and replaces the step's `args`. `input` starts the pipeline from a value instead of from the first call. Step arguments are data with the same `${` and object key limits as `aether_call`, and every step runs under this call's DSH file policy. When a job registry and live owning agent are available and promoteOnTimeout is enabled, timeoutMs bounds only the foreground wait: expiry returns the original job id without stopping or repeating the operation. Collect its final canonical JSON outcome with job_output; use job_kill to stop it. executionTimeoutMs is the independent hard runtime limit, also capped by the deployment's maxBackgroundRuntimeMs. Omitted hard limits mean no outer runtime cap when that deployment cap is zero; native proc_run timeout_ms is unchanged. Explicit call cancellation stops and awaits the owned run. Without ownership/jobs, with promotion disabled, or if admission is refused before execution, the foreground wait remains a kill deadline. A result over the deployment's complete-result budget is retained whole and returned as an id you read with `aether_result_page`, which never runs the program again; when this deployment cannot retain it, the call fails loudly and names the narrowing remedy instead of returning a partial value. An access the DSH file policy denies is final for this call: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

steps.description: Steps in execution order; at least one is required.

builtin.description: Flat native builtin name this step calls.

args.description: Positional arguments for this step; JSON data only.

select.description: Dotted field path read from each element of this step's result, for example "name" or "meta.size".

predicate.description: AetherShell expression passed to this step's builtin as `fn(x) => <predicate>`; replaces this step's args.

input.description: Value that starts the pipeline; omit it to start from the first step's call. An explicit null is rejected because the native request reads it as "no input" rather than the None value — seed None with aether_eval instead.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

timeoutMs.description: Foreground wait in milliseconds, capped by maxTimeoutMs. With job ownership and promotion enabled, expiry hands off the same execution; otherwise it is a kill deadline.

executionTimeoutMs.description: Independent positive hard execution deadline in milliseconds. Omitted, only maxBackgroundRuntimeMs applies (zero means no outer cap). Native proc_run timeout_ms remains independent.

initial.name: aether_result_page
initial.description: Read one page of a result this deployment retained because it was too large to return inline. `aether_call`, `aether_pipeline`, and `aether_eval` report such a result as an id and its shape; this tool returns its content one bounded page at a time. Paging reads the stored value and never runs the program again, so no side effect of the original call is repeated. Format `items` (the default) pages an array by whole elements and a record by whole fields; format `json` pages the canonical JSON encoding by UTF-8 byte offset, which also reads one element larger than a whole page. `offset`, `shown`, `total`, and `nextOffset` are counted in the returned `unit`, so pass back the previous page's `nextOffset` rather than computing an offset yourself. A result is private to the agent that produced it, is released when it expires idle, and is released when you pass `drop`.

id.description: Retrieval id of the retained result to read.

offset.description: Element index (format `items`) or UTF-8 byte offset (format `json`) to start at; defaults to the beginning. Pass back a previous page's `nextOffset`.

limit.description: Most elements, fields, or bytes to include. The page budget bounds the result either way.

maxBytes.description: Most bytes this page may occupy; defaults to the deployment's maxResultBytes and cannot exceed it.

format.description: `items` pages a container by whole elements or fields; `json` pages the canonical JSON encoding by UTF-8 byte offset.

drop.description: Release the retained result instead of reading it. Takes no other argument besides `id`.

initial.name: aether_session_close
initial.description: Close one of this agent's persistent AetherShell sessions and terminate its interpreter process. The native session is asked to close first, and the process is terminated afterwards whatever the interpreter answered, so a closed session never keeps running. Closing needs no new policy grant and always releases the process. Closing an id this agent does not hold reports `closed: false` and changes nothing; another agent's session is refused.

session_id.description: Opaque session id returned by aether_session_open.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_eval
initial.description: Evaluate one AetherShell program inside a persistent session and return its typed value. Unlike `aether_eval`, the program runs in the session's own long-lived process, so variables, functions, the current directory, and the environment all persist between calls and modules such as `file.read("notes.txt")` are available. A session is one real interpreter process on this host, holding native mutable state (variables, functions, the current directory, and the process environment) that survives between calls. That separation is the interpreter's own: two sessions do not share variables, functions, or a working directory, but they share the host itself, so files, network access, and every external service are common to all of them and to this machine. The plugin does not checkpoint interpreter state and does not replay commands, so nothing survives reopening a session and a session does not outlive the plugin or the harness process; the programs you send still read and write real host files. The code you send really runs, with real effects on this host. Its file writes and deletes run under the calling session's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control; the interpreter's own `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. The interpreter's evaluation surface is broad and is not restricted to builtin names. A failing program does not roll back what earlier statements in the same call already did. Requests carry a host-random nonce, so output the program prints is returned as bounded `logs` rather than mistaken for a result. One evaluation runs at a time per session. A call that reaches its deadline or is cancelled terminates the whole session process, because the interpreter cannot abandon a running command; open a new session to continue. An access the DSH file policy denies is final: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

session_id.description: Opaque session id returned by aether_session_open.

code.description: AetherShell program text: an expression, a lambda, or a sequence of statements executed in the session.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_list
initial.description: List the persistent AetherShell sessions this agent currently holds, with each one's opaque id, label, working directory, state, and file-policy mode. Sessions the calling session's DSH file policy no longer matches are closed here and reported as destroyed rather than shown as usable. Pass `usage: true` to add the interpreter's own evaluation and token counters for each live session, which costs one request per session. Another agent's sessions are never listed. An access the DSH file policy denies is final: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

usage.description: Also read each live session's counters from the interpreter (one request per session).

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_open
initial.description: Open a persistent AetherShell session and return an opaque session id. A session is one real interpreter process on this host, holding native mutable state (variables, functions, the current directory, and the process environment) that survives between calls. That separation is the interpreter's own: two sessions do not share variables, functions, or a working directory, but they share the host itself, so files, network access, and every external service are common to all of them and to this machine. The plugin does not checkpoint interpreter state and does not replay commands, so nothing survives reopening a session and a session does not outlive the plugin or the harness process; the programs you send still read and write real host files. The code you send really runs, with real effects on this host. Its file writes and deletes run under the calling session's DSH file policy, which governs writes and deletes rather than file reads, network access, or process control; the interpreter's own `sh` switch starts off as a convenience default, not a boundary. The interpreter's evaluation surface is broad and is not restricted to builtin names. Use `aether_session_eval` to run programs in it. Sessions are private to the agent that opened them, the deployment caps how many one agent may hold, and an idle session is closed automatically. The returned handle carries the DSH file policy it was opened under; if that policy later changes the session is closed rather than reused. An access the DSH file policy denies is final: retrying the same effect through another tool or shell is not a workaround, this plugin offers no in-turn escalation field, grants no permission automatically, and retries nothing with a native approval token — the user must change the policy explicitly for that effect to be allowed.

cwd.description: Working directory for the interpreter process. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

name.description: Optional label echoed by aether_session_list so you can tell sessions apart.

timeoutMs.description: Deadline in milliseconds before this plugin terminates the session process. The deployment applies its configured default and cap.

initial.name: aether_session_read
initial.description: Drain the output a persistent AetherShell session has written since the last drain, without running a program. A session may host a child or a service that keeps writing while no call is in flight, and every `aether_session_eval` already returns the output it saw; this tool reads whatever is left. Output is delivered exactly once: a second read with nothing new reports an empty result. Reading a session that has a call in flight is refused, because that output belongs to the call. Reading a closed or unknown session reports that the id is not open. Bounded like every other log, with the complete stream path when the retained tail was cut.

session_id.description: Opaque session id returned by aether_session_open.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: edit
initial.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: exit_plan_mode
initial.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

initial.name: get_goal
initial.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: interrupt_agent

initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

initial.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

initial.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

initial.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

initial.name: todo_write
initial.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

initial.name: update_goal
initial.description: Update the current goal.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

initial.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
